clue.text: Food from packet I agree to avoid

parts.note: a packet is slang for a lot of money, as is a bomb
aye or ay is an old word of assent
to duck is to dodge or avoid

explanation.surface: Someone eats from a packet of food they would rather avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: Bombay duck is not a duck at all: it is a dried fish served with curries. 'Packet' and 'bomb' are both British slang for a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay duck is dried salted fish eaten as a relish, so it is a food.

clue.text: Book a church organist

explanation.surface: A church organist books a slot to play.
explanation.definitionFit: J. S. Bach was a famous organist as well as a composer, so he exemplifies the definition.

clue.text: Victor in TV show left after first person pulled out

indicators.note: the word left is placed after the first person, signalled by after

parts.note: the first-person pronoun gives me
to have drawn a weapon is to have pulled it out

explanation.surface: A winner on a television show leaves after the first contestant withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a winner, but it is the first name of the grumpy hero of the British sitcom One Foot in the Grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Meldrew is the curmudgeonly lead character of the BBC sitcom One Foot in the Grave.

clue.text: Stress concealing identity by lying is clumsy?

indicators.note: concealing means the stress word wraps around and hides the identity letters

parts.note: stress on a syllable is an accent
ID is short for identity
lying flat on one's front is being prone

explanation.surface: A suspect hides his identity by lying, and is clumsy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply joins the two parts. The question mark marks the definition as a loose description: a clumsy person tends to have mishaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forever having mishaps through awkwardness is described as prone to accidents.

clue.text: Study getting to bottom of dull poet

indicators.note: in a down clue the study word goes to the bottom of, that is after, the dull word

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Studying gets to the root of what makes a dull poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was an English poet and Poet Laureate of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Cold meat then beef sandwiches in rising Alpine resort

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ham is a meat

indicators.note: sandwiches means the beef animal goes on either side of the other letters

parts.note: an ox is a beef animal

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word in is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A cold-meat-and-beef sandwich is served in a ski resort as the chairlift rises.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads a piece upwards, so only the little word 'in' is turned before the beef goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamonix is a famous ski and climbing resort below Mont Blanc in the French Alps.

clue.text: Drugs officer gets report of needle

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the sound of the word is what counts

parts.note: to needle someone is to nark or annoy them

explanation.surface: A narcotics officer gets word of a hypodermic needle found at a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nark' is British slang for to irritate; it sounds the same as narc, the American slang for a drugs agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics agent, an officer of the drug squad.

clue.text: Means to order a rum or finish off brandy

indicators.note: to order means to arrange, so these words are put into a new arrangement
finish off picks the final letter of the word brandy

explanation.surface: A customer is told how to order a rum or polish off a brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' makes ARMOUR from A, RUM and OR; 'finish off' adds Y, the last letter of 'brandy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is a stock of resources, as in the tools in one's armoury, hence one's means.

clue.text: Support calls for a ventricle to be transplanted

indicators.note: transplanted suggests surgery moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heart patient is told the ventricle must be transplanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls for' is a link; 'to be transplanted' rearranges A plus VENTRICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam fixed at one end that supports a balcony or bridge span.

clue.text: Reluctant to hold tongue, being in pain

indicators.note: to hold means the reluctant word contains the tongue word

parts.note: coy means shy or reluctant
to lick is to tongue

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to keep quiet because they are suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold tongue' suggests keeping silent, but tongue here is the verb, lick.
explanation.definitionFit: A colicky baby suffers from abdominal cramps, so it is in pain.

clue.text: White poacher does tramp through winding lane

indicators.note: the tramp goes through, that is inside, the twisted lane
winding means the letters of the word lane twist into a new order

parts.note: bum is slang for a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A white poacher sends a tramp along a winding lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' makes ALEN from LANE, and BUM goes through it. The poacher is an egg poacher, who cooks the white of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is egg white, which someone poaching an egg cooks.

clue.text: Poor nun stopping by with Franklin's Tale character

parts.note: Benjamin was the first name of the American statesman Franklin

indicators.note: stopping means the scrambled nun letters plug the gap in the word by

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, signalling the letters of the word nun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A destitute nun stops off with a character from Chaucer's Franklin's Tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Franklin's Tale' is from Chaucer, but the Tale here is Beatrix Potter's Tale of Benjamin Bunny. 'Poor' makes UNN from NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Bunny is the rabbit hero of Beatrix Potter's The Tale of Benjamin Bunny.

clue.text: Ms Jones with private place in Caribbean

parts.note: Bridget Jones is the singleton heroine of Helen Fielding's diary novels
one's own is private, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Ms Jones holidays with a private villa somewhere in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridgetown is the capital of Barbados, an island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Heard question about identity of Cockney killer

indicators.note: heard means the clue words describe something spoken, so only the sound counts

parts.note: a Londoner asking who someone is says something like oo's 'e, dropping the h sounds

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a question about who a Cockney murderer is.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney drops the h of 'Who's he?', giving a sound like the name of the Israeli submachine gun. Cockney is the dialect of working-class East London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is a submachine gun, a weapon and so a killer.

clue.text: Sweet child eating cake but ignoring a rugby ball might be

parts.note: a drop is a small boiled sweet, as in a pear drop

indicators.note: eating means the child word swallows the shortened cake

parts.note: kid is informal for a child

indicators.note: ignoring means one letter, the a, is left out of the cake word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child with a sweet eats cake while ignoring the rugby ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring a' removes A from CAKE to leave CKE, which KID eats.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop kick is a kick made as the dropped ball bounces, so a rugby ball might be drop-kicked.

clue.text: Runs outstanding Olympic event

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a debt that is outstanding is still owing

explanation.surface: A runner hits form in an Olympic event.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing races in boats are held at the Olympic Games, a sport of the summer programme.

clue.text: By hiding in private entrance, obtaining this much information?

parts.note: a private is a common soldier, a GI in American usage

indicators.note: hiding in means the word by goes inside the soldier and gate letters

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lurking in a private doorway, someone gathers this much intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like an adjective for the entrance; it is the soldier, GI.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigabyte is a unit of computer data, about a billion bytes, so a quantity of information.

clue.text: Film has dwarf and sailors in also

parts.note: Doc is one of the Seven Dwarfs in Snow White

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the word for also

parts.note: too means also
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A film features a dwarf and some sailors too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'and' are links; Doc is one of the Seven Dwarfs and RN the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr. No is the 1962 film, the first in the James Bond series.

clue.text: Bear with twin producing rubbish

indicators.note: with twin means the bear's name comes paired with an identical copy

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear, Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A teddy and its twin are turned into rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' is the verb here, to dismiss as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an idea scornfully is to rubbish it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Sort of marmalade showing lack of variety — and variable

parts.note: O, nothing, stands for a lack
a range is a variety, as in a range of goods
Y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: A marmalade showing no variety and inconsistent quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is made from citrus, so one tasting of orange can be described this way.

clue.text: West Indies' best bowlers liked England's openers to shake!

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies cricket team

indicators.note: openers, like opening batsmen, are the first letters of these words

explanation.surface: England's openers tremble before the West Indies' best fast bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first batsmen in; here they are the first letters of 'best bowlers liked England's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wibble is an informal word meaning to wobble, tremble or quiver.

clue.text: Shoot one protecting race in African state

indicators.note: protecting means the shoot and one letters surround and shelter the race

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
a run is a race
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shooter guards a race in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like firing a gun; it is a bud on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Burundi is a small landlocked country in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Requirement to be in police once upset minority?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: the RUC, the Royal Ulster Constabulary, was the police force of Northern Ireland until 2001
a few are a minority

explanation.surface: Police of the past impose a restriction that upsets a minority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RUC into CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order that people stay indoors after a set hour.

clue.text: Girl is one Bill rebuffed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the bill word is turned around

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A girl is the one whom Bill turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an advertisement, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a feminine given name, so it serves as an example of a girl, the usual crossword use of that word.

clue.text: Is more than unsure tomb should be disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is uncertain whether a tomb should be disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be greater in number than another group is to exceed it in count.

clue.text: Girl lifting light ebony boxes

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the letters are read upwards, backwards
boxes means the words light ebony contain the letters

explanation.surface: A girl lifts a light ebony box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' finds HTEB inside 'light ebony', and 'lifting' turns it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth.

clue.text: Drink when under pressure to fulfil role as monarch, following king, say

indicators.note: following places the role and monarch letters after those for king and say

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
say means for example, EG
to fulfil a role is to be it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A drink taken while under pressure to play the monarch after a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Keg beer is served from a pressurised keg. ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Keg beer is kept in sealed casks and dispensed under gas pressure, a drink served that way.

clue.text: Intended to bring in new sponsor

indicators.note: to bring in means the intended word takes the new letter inside it

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiance

explanation.surface: An engaged couple bring in a new backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like a verb, meant; it is the noun, a fiance.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a venture is to fund or sponsor it, both verbs.

clue.text: Back down, accepting year is shorter time period

indicators.note: accepting means the reversed sad word takes the year letter inside
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: down means sad, depressed

explanation.surface: Feeling low, someone accepts that a year is a shorter span than hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns SAD into DAS, which takes in Y. 'down' looks like a direction; it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Days are units of time each shorter than a year, so they are a shorter time period.

clue.text: Make a path through scrub

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
a way is a path
with means by means of, as through does

explanation.surface: A path is cleared through the scrubland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrub' looks like rough vegetation; it is the verb, to cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub plans is to cancel them, to get rid of them entirely.
